A1.justification: Both PDFs contain the same MoRAS research work, with readable main text, equations, figures, tables, and supplementary material. Content can be reliably matched despite extensive reformatting and changed pagination.

before.justification: v3 reports original safety, utility, computational-overhead, and ablation results, including Tables 1–12 and supplementary analyses.

after.justification: v4 retains these original experimental results, including benchmark comparisons, attention analyses, and supplementary robustness evaluations.

M1.justification: Sections 3.2–3.4 and Algorithm 1 retain the same query reformulation, exponentially weighted risk evaluation, and adaptive activation steering. Describing visual contexts as brief text summaries clarifies the existing method.

E1.justification: The safety and utility benchmarks are unchanged. Supplementary coverage, including XSTest, OR-Bench, suffix injection, alternative object datasets, and calibration sources, was already present in v3.

E2.justification: Corresponding comparisons retain Vanilla, CoCA, ECSO, FigStep, ETA, AutoSteer, and ASTRA. The refusal-vector comparison with Arditi et al. in Table 7 and fixed-strength comparisons in Table 12 are also unchanged.

E3.justification: Evaluation settings remain the same, including model backbones, benchmark subsets, judges, attack settings, and calibration sample counts. Both versions use gamma = 0.3 and N = 3 and retain the same supplementary baseline sweeps.

E4.justification: Both versions contain the same stage ablation, hyperparameter sensitivity, attention/FDR analyses, calibration-source tests, refusal-vector comparisons, suffix-attack evaluation, overhead breakdowns, and qualitative steering examples.

E5.justification: Neither version reports repeated-run counts, seeds, confidence intervals, error bars, or formal significance tests. No uncertainty-reporting practice is added or revised.

E6.justification: Matched tables and figures retain their numerical results and qualitative findings. For example, Table 1 reports identical LLaVA-1.5-7B MoRAS ASRs of 7.6, 2.8, and 2.6 on SPA-VL, FigStep, and MM-Safety, respectively, and MM-Vet utility of 30.5.

T1.justification: Equations 1–9 retain the same FDR, prototype, similarity, risk-score, steering, and attention definitions. Mathematical differences in extraction reflect typesetting; no assumptions, derivations, or proofs are substantively changed.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction, and conclusion retain the same attention-based motivation and safety, utility, generalization, and efficiency claims. The headline 19.4% ASR reduction, 126.6-fold lower pre-deployment overhead, and 1.6-fold faster throughput claims remain unchanged.

C2.justification: The interpretations concerning visual grounding, risk estimation, calibration generalization, and safety–utility trade-offs remain unchanged. The expanded ethics paragraph reiterates existing residual vulnerabilities and generic misuse concerns without introducing a substantive new limitation.

D1.justification: v4 newly states code availability and supplies a repository link in the abstract. References also add direct access links for Caltech 101 and the LLM Red Teaming Dataset. Existing prompts, hyperparameters, hardware, and implementation procedures are retained.

R1.justification: Both versions cite the same 57 works and retain the same research positioning. Alphabetical renumbering and publication-metadata updates, including Safety-Tuned LLaMAs, do not introduce different prior work.

P1.justification: v4 makes limited wording clarifications, expands ethics and acknowledgements, and refines supplementary cross-references. Section 3.2 corrects the Figure 4 comparison from green-versus-yellow to orange-versus-yellow. The scientific narrative and section order remain intact.

P2.justification: The entire document adopts a different template, changing typography, margins, headers, captions, and figure/table sizing and placement. For example, Figures 14 and 15 move from separate pages to a shared page. These substantial layout changes preserve the underlying displays and results.

improvement.justification: v4 modestly improves reproducibility information through explicit code and dataset access pointers and corrects the misleading Figure 4 color reference in Section 3.2. The methods and empirical evidence remain unchanged, so the extensive reformatting does not constitute a substantial scientific improvement.
